answer.rationale: The mandate is an 18% cost cut with no added delivery risk. memory_c2 already shows the low-cost vendor delivered accurate invoicing and quick onboarding, supporting a clean switch. memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing, which could deepen the cost saving if the new vendor is willing. I pull both to confirm the cost figures and onboarding details before committing. I do not add a second source or defer because capacity allows only one action and the contract lapses in 14 days; deferring risks a gap. I flag the 94% line-utilization as the key downside risk and will keep the incumbent warm for 90 days as a contingency during the transition. If memory_c2 shows material onboarding friction or if the quoted price fails to clear the 18% threshold after verification, I fall back to negotiate_terms with the incumbent instead.
